fractalNodeStatus.description:
FractalNodeStatus is the mirror image of ShadowStatus: it describes this
printer's own Fractal node, so it is set only for a printer this instance
owns and bridges, and omitted for a shadow (whose freshness ShadowStatus
already reports) and for any printer nothing bridges. Nothing bridges when
Fractal is off, or when a uuid is absent from fractal.owned_device_ids.
OK means the node is up and an
ancestor mirroring this printer is being told so; STALE means it is not.

Per-printer on purpose. /api/server/info's fractal_enabled answers the same
question for the instance, which is not enough to make a claim about one
printer: a printer can be connected to an instance running Fractal and
still be bridged nowhere, because its uuid was never configured.

remotePath.description:
RemotePath and ShadowStatus are set only for a printer mirrored from
another prusa-connect instance via the Fractal protocol (both omitted
for a locally-connected printer). ShadowStatus is the Fractal sync
status (EMPTY/OK/STALE).

tools.description:
Tools is the per-slot tool inventory keyed by 0-based slot id ("0",
"0.0" for an MMU feeder). Omitted for a printer that has reported none.

fractal_enabled.description:
FractalEnabled reports whether this instance is running with Fractal at
all (config-enabled, built with the "fractal" tag, and past a successful
Initialize). It is false in every build or config where no Fractal node
exists. An instance-level capability: whether any one printer is actually
bridged is a different question, answered per printer by
PrinterResponse.FractalNodeStatus, since a printer can be attached to an
instance where this is true and still be bridged nowhere.

materialPackageInstance.description:
MaterialPackageInstance carries the firmware-reported abbreviation; it is
set only when MaterialState is PRESENT. The json tag documents the field
for Swagger. The absent, null and present encoding is done in MarshalJSON.
